editorial:
The Adventures of Robin Hood is Warner Bros.' 1938 Technicolor swashbuckler, directed by Michael Curtiz and William Keighley. Errol Flynn and Olivia de Havilland star, and Erich Wolfgang Korngold wrote the score. The Library of Congress added it to the National Film Registry in 1995. A creator would want it for its sword fights, its sets and its Korngold music, all of which are in constant demand for clips and homages.

The rights trap is that nobody has shown this film to be free. The queue flagged it as likely not renewed, but I could not confirm that against the 1965 and 1966 renewal records, and Warner has kept the film in commercial circulation. Until someone checks those records by hand, treat the print, the Korngold track, and any Warner restoration or home-video master as protected. Do not reuse clips on the strength of the queue's guess.
faq: Is The Adventures of Robin Hood (1938) in the public domain?

Not established. The film was released in 1938, so its status depends on whether the copyright was renewed in the 28th year. I could not confirm a renewal or its absence in the Catalog of Copyright Entries. Check the 1965 and 1966 volumes before reusing any footage.
Can I use the Korngold score or a Warner restoration if the film turns out to be free?

Not automatically. The original track normally shares the film's status. A Warner restoration or newer remaster can add protected material. Ripping a copy-protected disc can also violate 17 U.S.C. 1201 whatever the film's status.
